label: Copy phase of length-9 sequences, mainly the 3rd output step (t=11), token-modulated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>), only on inputs that repeat an earlier token (in_first=0), and almost only in long sequences (L=9 holds 83% of mass, L>=8 holds 96%; never for L<=5). Within L=9 it peaks at t=11 (recall_idx 2, prev2_tok=<DEL>, ~47% of mass) and again at the last steps t=16-17, with smaller bumps at t=10 and 12. Which token is being re-input strongly changes the firing rate: z (7.5x), x, s, f, 0, g, e are favored, while o and c are rarely active. Even so, precision stays low (~27% at L=9,t=11; ~72% if you also restrict to the favored tokens, but then recall is 21%). That suggests it depends on a hidden-state conjunction that no simple predicate captures. Activations are tiny (max 0.011). The largest come at z inputs late in L=9 copies.
